steps.speaker: arkus
steps.text:
(upright on the mended bunk, stiff, bandaged wrong in two places)
You are the ones who carried me. Good. I hate owing strangers.

steps.speaker: player
steps.text: You were on the road past the near forest. A dire wolf.

steps.speaker: arkus
steps.text:
The wolf. Yes.
I went in to prove something. I came out like this. What I carried was not enough. Bad steel breaks when you need it to hold.

steps.speaker: arkus
steps.text:
(tests the arm, winces, does not complain)
You killed it, then. With better luck than sense, probably. The next thing out of that forest will be worse. You will want a forge. I can build one. I know metal — it is the one thing the rite did not take from me.

options.text: We have a place for a smithy. It's yours.

steps.speaker: arkus
steps.text: Then it is settled. I start when the frame is up.

options.text: You could barely stand a moment ago.

steps.speaker: arkus
steps.text: I mended a spearhead once with a broken hand. Standing is optional. Straight steel is not.

steps.speaker: arkus
steps.text:
(glances down at their own botched bandages)
And this — whoever wrapped me meant well and did it wrong. You have no proper place to mend the hurt. There will be more of us coming back like I did. Build somewhere to put them. A sickbed, before you need one and do not have it.

steps.speaker: tharr
steps.text:
(from the doorway)
A forge and an infirmary.
The table can hold both.
